status_reason: Material (exhaust gas), quantity (CO2 and CH4) and location (hot duct) are known, but the probe interface, duct conditions and concentrations are not.
answer: A silica-fiber probe cannot carry the CO2 and CH4 absorption bands, which lie at about 4-10 µm. The method to test first is mid-infrared gas absorption through a PIR fiber (3-17 µm) to a gas interface designed for the duct. Duct conditions, concentrations and the interface are unknown, so a laboratory test comes before any installation.

inline.headline: Test MIR gas absorption for CO2 and CH4 in a lab gas cell first, then at the duct with a PIR fiber interface
inline.probe: Gas-absorption interface (gas cell or duct probe) with PIR fiber, to be designed and tested
inline.install: Measurement point in the hot exhaust duct; no installation is described yet, so the interface must be designed
inline.test_against: Independent laboratory analysis of extracted gas samples
inline.not_final_because: CO2 and CH4 bands lie beyond silica fiber; no duct interface is described; duct temperature, pressure, dust, concentrations and interfering gases are unknown; the sources give no gas accuracy or detection limits

problems.text: A silica-fiber probe (transmits about 350-2400 nm) cannot carry the CO2 and CH4 absorption bands at about 4-10 µm.
Gas measurement is only briefly covered by the sources, and no gas-cell or duct installation is described, so the interface must be designed and tested.
A single fiber probe does not settle the method: each method needs its own interface, and the task decides the technique.
Fiber choice matters: hollow waveguides have low NA and couple poorly to FTIR spectrometers, while PIR fibers couple better, so the fiber must be checked against the spectrometer.

methods.why: Mid-IR is highly sensitive for gases, and the CO2 and CH4 bands at 4-10 µm lie inside the PIR fiber range.
Silica fiber does not transmit the 4-10 µm gas bands.
Raman signals are weak and need special probes and filters, and no gas-phase Raman data are supplied.
Fluorimetry needs secondary emission from the sample, and most chemicals do not fluoresce.

questions.q: What are the gas temperature, pressure, dust load and moisture at the measurement point?
questions.why: These set the interface design and whether the probe and fiber can be installed; dust and vibration on the process floor affect instruments.

questions.q: What CO2 and CH4 concentration ranges and accuracy are required, and how fast must readings update?
questions.why: The method and path length depend on the concentration range, and the sources give no gas detection limits, so the target must come from the client.

questions.q: What optical path length through the gas is possible at the duct, and can a probe be inserted into it?
questions.why: Path choice follows the absorbance level, so the path length must be fixed before testing.

questions.q: Which other gases are present, such as H2O, CO, SO2 or NH3?
questions.why: Their bands lie in the same 4-10 µm region, so they can overlap with CO2 and CH4.

experiment.objective: Establish whether MIR absorption through a PIR fiber can resolve CO2 and CH4 under duct-like conditions.
steps: Set up a heated lab gas cell at the duct's temperature and pressure (values from the client), coupled by PIR fiber to an MIR spectrometer.
Record spectra over 4-10 µm for pure CO2 and CH4 and for mixtures with the other gases present.
Check PIR fiber transmission across the measured range and its coupling to the spectrometer.
Compare readings against independent laboratory analysis of extracted gas samples, not the instrument's own calibration.
Move the interface to a duct test point and repeat the comparison.

pathway.key_features: CO2 and CH4 absorption bands at about 4-10 µm; no spectrum is supplied, so the features must be found in lab trials.
pathway.path_reason: Lab trials on the client's gas conditions come first in the AFS pathway.

multispectral.why: The sources show two-method gains for complex media and tissues, but none for gas-phase CO2 and CH4; Raman signals are weak and fluorescence needs fluorescent substances, so no pair is justified yet.
multispectral.test: Test MIR alone first; add a second method only if MIR alone fails the client's criteria.

assumptions: The client's probe is assumed to be a silica-fiber probe, since the enquiry does not name the fiber.
Duct temperature, pressure, dust, moisture and gas concentrations are unknown.
PIR range is 3-17 µm in the fiber table and 3-16 µm on another page; check the vendor datasheet.
Other gases such as H2O, CO, SO2 and NH3 may be present.
